holidays.name: National Pig Day
holidays.description: Oink! This is a day to celebrate one of the smartest, snuggliest and most underrated barnyard animals. Fans mark it with pig-themed snacks, piggy crafts, visits to sanctuaries and plenty of bacon-free admiration for the humble hog.
holidays.origin: National Pig Day was created in 1972 by sisters Ellen Stanley and Mary Lynne Rave. They wanted to see pigs recognized as intelligent, companionable animals and to give them more respect.
holidays.funFact: Pigs are widely regarded as among the smartest domestic animals. Studies have shown they can learn to play simple video games with a joystick.

holidays.name: National Peanut Butter Lover's Day
holidays.description: A sticky, nutty salute to the pantry staple that has glued together generations of sandwiches. Celebrate with a PB&J, peanut butter cookies, or a spoon straight from the jar. No judgment.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on food-holiday calendars for spreading the love of peanut butter.
holidays.funFact: Under U.S. food regulations, a product has to be at least 90 percent peanuts to be sold as peanut butter.

holidays.name: World Compliment Day
holidays.description: A global nudge to hand out sincere, kind words to friends, coworkers and strangers. The idea is that a single compliment can brighten someone's day and set off a chain reaction of good vibes.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that encourages people everywhere to give genuine compliments. It has been celebrated on March 1 as a simple way to spread kindness.
holidays.funFact: Compliments are free, calorie-free and endlessly renewable. Giving one often lifts the giver's mood as much as the receiver's.
